nodes.title: English First Additional Language
nodes.description: English First Additional Language for Grade 8 covering Listening and Speaking, Reading and Viewing, Writing and Presenting, and Language Structures and Conventions.

nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: Term 1: Short story, poem, novel, speech, newspaper article. FAT1: Oral — prepared reading (10 pts). FAT2: Essay — narrative/reflective (30 pts). FAT3: Literature and language test (60 pts).

nodes.title: Short Story, Novel and Poetry
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: listen to a short story or novel extract; identify main and supporting ideas; make notes; summarise; discuss. Oral reading preparation (FAT1 begins). Reading and Viewing: short story — literary features: character, plot, conflict, setting, theme, point of view; novel — introduction, parts of a book, character analysis; poem — structure, imagery, figures of speech, tone, mood. Writing and Presenting: narrative/reflective essay (FAT2, 30 pts, weeks 7-8); paragraph writing: topic sentence, body, concluding sentence; writing process. Language Structures and Conventions: word classes revision; complex sentences; tense review; punctuation; idioms; vocabulary building.

nodes.title: Newspaper Article and Transactional Writing
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: formal speech listening — identify purpose, tone, audience; summarise key points; evaluate effectiveness. Reading and Viewing: newspaper/magazine article — features: headline, byline, lead paragraph, inverted pyramid structure; editorial/opinion column; fact vs opinion; bias; persuasive language devices. Writing and Presenting: transactional — investigative newspaper article or editorial; formal register. Language Structures and Conventions: passive voice; reported speech; conditional sentences; formal language conventions; spelling rules.

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: Term 2: Novel, drama, folk tale, advertisement/poster. FAT4: Transactional short task (10 pts). FAT5: Mid-year exam — literature/language test (60 pts).

nodes.title: Novel and Drama
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: drama reading; role play or panel discussion on social issues; group discussion. Reading and Viewing: novel — deeper character, theme, writer's craft, symbolism; drama text — dramatic conventions, stage directions, dialogue, conflict; folk tale — oral tradition, moral, cultural context. Writing and Presenting: descriptive essay or creative response; summary writing; recount. Language Structures and Concerns: relative clauses; conditional sentences; sentence variety; paragraph cohesion; figurative language; punctuation.

nodes.title: Visual Texts and Transactional Writing
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: listen to an advertisement or visual presentation; identify purpose, target audience; evaluate effectiveness. Reading and Viewing: visual text — advertisement or poster: visual elements, language, AIDA model, persuasive techniques; folk tale analysis. Writing and Presenting: transactional — design/write an advertisement or review (FAT4 short transactional, 10 pts). Language Structures and Conventions: modal verbs; language of persuasion; formal and informal register; vocabulary extension; spelling conventions.

nodes.title: Term 3
nodes.description: Term 3: Short story, Creative Writing Project. FAT6: CWP Research (20 pts) + Write-up (30 pts). FAT7: Oral — CWP Presentation (20 pts, begin T3 conclude T4). FAT8: Response to Literature (30 pts).

nodes.title: Short Story and Creative Writing Project
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: listen to a short story/information text; note taking; begin preparing CWP oral presentation (FAT7, 20 pts). Reading and Viewing: literary text — short story or drama; research reading for CWP; visual texts for comprehension. Writing and Presenting: CWP Phase 1 Research (FAT6, 20 pts, weeks 3-4): research notes, bibliography, graphic organisers; CWP Phase 2 Write-up (FAT6, 30 pts, week 6): produce final product in chosen genre. FAT8 Response to Literature (30 pts): poetry (compulsory), novel/drama, short story/folk tale. Language Structures and Conventions: genre-specific language; vocabulary for chosen genre; essay structure; critical language.

nodes.title: Diary Entry, Multimedia and Oral Preparation
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: prepare and practice oral presentation (CWP); peer feedback and discussion. Reading and Viewing: diary entry or multimedia text — features, format, personal and emotive language; visual comprehension. Writing and Presenting: diary entry or personal journal connected to project content; notes for oral presentation. Language Structures and Conventions: personal and reflective language; first person writing; emotional and descriptive vocabulary.

nodes.title: Term 4
nodes.description: Term 4: Conclude oral (FAT7); instructions, forms/questionnaires; FAT9 transactional (10 pts); revision; end-of-year exam.

nodes.title: Transactional Texts, Oral Completion and Revision
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: conclude FAT7 oral presentations; peer assessment. Reading and Viewing: information texts — instructions, newspaper article; forms and questionnaires — features, format, purpose; revision of all genres and text types. Writing and Presenting: instructions; questionnaire/form; FAT9 transactional short task (10 pts, for exam). Language Structures and Conventions: comprehensive revision of all grammar, vocabulary, punctuation and spelling; end-of-year examination practice; past papers.
